steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Breathe in—

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hffff—

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Breath out—

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Phew—

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Here. Eat this.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Okay—Gah, so sour...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: At least it's edible, right? You'll get used to it.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: And here. This too.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Awgh—Huh? How come this nut is hollow?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Like a bubble?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Mm... yeah.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: The locals call them 'bubbles.' You hardly feel anything when you eat them, but they're very important for climbing these mountains.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Do you feel better now? Does your head still hurt?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Mm—I'm fine now. These fruits and nuts are way better than altitude sickness pills, at least.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: So do you know how they work?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: No. But does it really matter, as long as they do?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Of course it does. I gotta jot this down and bring some samples back with me. My colleagues in pharmaceutical R&D would love to hear about this.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Did you bring any of those pills?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: For altitude sickness? Of course.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: You should take a look at the active ingredients.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: (Rummages through baggage)

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Here they are!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Main ingredients... wild sourberries and bubblenut extract... You mean...?!

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: One of Sami's primary exports to Columbia is raw medicinal ingredients.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Although I hear your company plans to cut off all trade with us as soon as they figure out how to synthesize or cultivate them themselves.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Unfortunately for them, that will never happen. Not with something from Sami.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: You're saying we can't recreate the growth conditions in Columbia?

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: No, of course you can. But even if you did, what sprouts from the soil wouldn't be the same plants.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: For one very simple reason.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: (In Sami) Because everything is provided by Sami.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (In Sami) Everything is provided by Sami.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: (In broken Sami) Everything... provided... by Sami?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: You pick up languages quickly. When we first met, you needed Simone to translate for you whenever you wanted to say something about Sami.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hehe~

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Your Columbian's not bad at all either.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Arges speaks it well. That's why I can manage.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: I see the tree line. The mountainfolk won't bother us anymore.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Phew, finally. A place to have a good meal.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Do trees mean better food?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: The mountains have meat, but no fruit.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: The forest is different. There are all kinds of food there. Anything you could want to eat.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Whoa.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: (Pulls out notes and starts writing) 'Forest has abundant resources...'

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Typhon, is there a settlement nearby?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Yes, and it's a tribe with a tree.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Then they must have lived here in peace for many years.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: A tribe with a tree? What does that mean?

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Each forest tribe has their own clan tree.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: ...If they don't, then they must either be up-and-coming, or they managed to lose even their tree. Whichever the case, it's laughable.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Will this tribe listen to us?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I believe they're quite friendly.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: But either way, I can guarantee they will be more welcoming than the mountain tribes.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Huh? Really?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Of course. The mountain warriors fight the monsters in the north and the unfriendly Ursus all year round, so you can't blame them for being so uptight.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Some of them are less cold when they leave the frontlines for home.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Well, that's good to hear.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: So, how do the Sami usually categorize themselves?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: It's pretty easy to remember. The ones farthest to the north who live in the mountains are the mountainfolk, the ones who live in the middle in the forest and its surroundings are the forestfolk, and the ones who live in the wetlands to the far south are the marshfolk.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: What about you, then?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Me? I'm a hunter?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: A hunter? Uh, going by the classifications you just gave me, shouldn't it be based on what environment you're from?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Oh, that... I'm a Sarkaz. I don't have a fixed place to live, and I don't belong to a tribe. So naturally, I live outside the rules.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Then what about Simone?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Simone...? She—

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: I'm a Rhodes Islander.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Rhodes? I've never heard of an island like that here.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Is Rhodes Island another category here?

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Perhaps.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Here we are.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Whoa—

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: This tree... It's like... a vertical nomadic city!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I-I've never seen—

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: —I've gotta take a picture.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: It doesn't seem so different from last time, but—

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Why does it look like they're all moving things outside?

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) Welcome, friends.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (In Sami) Thank you for your hospitality, Attendant of the Tree. We came from the north. Would it be convenient for us to stay the night?

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) Of course, honorable shaman. We always enjoy receiving guests. In any other circumstances, your arrival would be reason enough for a feast.

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) Alas, as you can see, we are preparing to move from this land that has long been our home. We leave on the morrow.

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) You will find many of our houses on the Tree empty tonight. You and your companions may pick any of them to rest in. The Tree won't mind.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (In Sami) I thank the Tree and your tribe for your generosity.

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) You are very welcome. Please, come in.

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) Once you have settled down, please come to the ancestral home at the top of the Tree. We may have need of your wisdom.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (Nods)

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: We have their permission to stay the night. Let's pick... the house closest to the branch there.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hah... Finally, sleeping indoors.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Is that important?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: How else can you rest easy? Otherwise, you're up all night from worry.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Is that so... That's awfully picky of you.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: It's not. Let me explain—

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Waterproof pad... sleeping bag... there!

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Pft.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: What's so funny?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Hm? Oh, I just thought it was amusing that you put in all this effort just to sleep.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: We don't get this chance every day, so I'm gonna make the most of it and get as comfy as I can.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Want to try it yourself?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Me? No need. As long as I have my robe to wrap myself in, I can sleep anywhere.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I mean, sure, you could... But you could also get in this sleeping bag and close your eyes. It's sooo comfortable, you'll see.

spans.text: ... But you could also get in this sleeping bag and close your eyes. It's sooo comfortable, you'll see.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Really?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Can't hurt to give it a try, can it?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Alright...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Hup...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Just squeeze yourself in there. I won't zip it up.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Mm, it's soft. Like beast skin... But it feels lighter than that...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Mmm...

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: These are our rations for tonight.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Alright, thanks. You can leave Typhon's over here.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: What's wrong with her?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I had her try out my sleeping bag, and she fell asleep, just like that.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: I need to step out for a second and speak with the shaman here.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: If you want to go outside, you should take Typhon with you.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: The forestfolk may be friendlier, but they won't appreciate it if you don't follow their rules.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Okay, got it.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Have a safe trip, Simone!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hey... Typhon. Typhon?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: She seems pretty exhausted.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I'll just take a few photos from the doorway...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (In Sami) You requested my presence, ma'am?

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) Yes, yes. Thank goodness you've come.

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) Allow me to explain the situation. As you can see, we are preparing to move.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (In Sami) We encountered some trouble on our journey from the mountains. Are you facing similar issues here?

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) Indeed, indeed.

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) Thankfully, there are no victims yet, but my tribesmen tell me of a number of ill omens we've received.

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) Most importantly, there's this.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (In Sami) 'Korona,' 'Hreidr.'

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) Samivilinn is clear. Regardless of the reason, my tribe must depart for a more suitable home.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (In Sami) I understand.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (In Sami) But then, why did you summon me...?

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) Please take a look at this.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (In Sami) I mustn't. This is your tribe's register.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (In Sami) I am an outsider.

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) I understand your concerns, my friend.

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) I've lived in this forest ever since I was a child. As did my father, his father, and all of our ancestors.

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) But because we have lived such quiet, comfortable lives for so long, this register has become barely more than a symbol for us, an inheritance.

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) When I flip it open, I find myself unable to understand all of its words.

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) I've studied it with my family, and communicated with my ancestors in hopes of understanding of the symbols within.

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) But I feel as though we are still missing something.

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) You are a shaman too, are you not?

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (In Sami) I was.

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) As long as you were once, your wisdom will undoubtedly be of assistance to us, friend.

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) Please have a look. We need your advice.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Hah!

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Sleeping bags are actually pretty comfortable...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Magallan!

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Strange... Where is she?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Things seem pretty noisy outside...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Hm... 'Outlander...' 'touching the clan tree'?!

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Oh no, it has to be that birdbrain!

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Speak.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I'm sorry! I knew I couldn't take samples, but I had no idea I wasn't even supposed to touch it!

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: The tribe's tree is their oldest, most respected presence. Under normal circumstances, an outsider wouldn't even get the chance to stay in their tree houses.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Would you touch an ancient monument for no good reason? That, or... Do you have any wise elders where you're from?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hm... The President?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: President, okay. If you were to run up to your president and touch their face, how would others react?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I'd probably be tackled to the ground by secret service agents before I got within ten feet of him...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: It's like that, then.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Luckily, these people are peaceful. All they've done is talk behind your back. If we were anywhere more hotheaded, they might have taken an axe to your head.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I'm sorry...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Simone told you to take me with you when you go outside. How could you forget?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I just wanted to take a few pictures, but the tree looked like it had a nice texture, so I wanted to see it up close, and...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Wait, huh? You heard what she said? Weren't you asleep?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I could hear her while asleep.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Th-Then how come you didn't wake up when I called your name?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Because I was asleep.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Anyway, you've learned your lesson. Don't get hung up on it. Do you want to try some tasty fruits and nuts?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: They have any here?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I saw a lot of them in the forest.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Come, we'll pick as many as we can. Enough for Simone too. We can eat them on the road tomorrow.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Mm-hmm.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: You two are back?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Mmhmm!

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: We got some fresh fruits. Do you want any, Simone?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Mmmmmm?

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: We should rest now.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Magallan.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Mmm?

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Typhon, what did you feed her?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: It wasn't me. She picked some nuts and asked if they were poisonous. I said no, and before I could even finish, she'd stuffed her mouth full of them.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Silencing chestnuts?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: You should rest, then. A good night's sleep ought to fix it.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Good night.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Good night, Simone.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Mm mmmmm.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Mmmm!

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: What's wrong?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: You keep the sleeping bag. I don't need it.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Sweet dreams.
Magallan can still remember how fluffy and warm her sleeping bag was, and how rhythmic the breathing of those around her was.
It was a quiet, comfortable environment, just perfect for resting.
But the moment she opens her eyes, she finds herself in the forest.
A blanket of greenery drapes over her waist. The trees around her have shrouded the moonlight above. It is completely dark all around.
She feels thirsty, so she follows the sound of water to a stream. She bends down to drink from it.
Nothing is out of the ordinary. Everything is exactly as it should be, even when she sees the reflection in the water.
Even if the reflection in the water is that of—
A musbeast.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: *Squeak*

The night is dark, quiet, and full of terrors. Magallan instinctively senses danger. She quickly lies down and breezes through the bushes before climbing onto the tree marked with her secretions, the nest she calls home.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: *Squeak*!
It is safe there. There, she will find her kin, her family. She stands on the tree branch and squeals, waiting for a reply.
Nothing.
She hesitates a little, but in the end hops onto the tree trunk and back into her nest.
There, her mother is fast asleep in the shadows.
She wants to snuggle up to her, to get through the night in her embrace, but once her eyes adjust to the darkness, she finds only a scattered pile of beast bones.
The nest is very wide and very dark, almost like there's something waiting for her.
Waiting for her to come home.
Waiting for her to lower her guard.
Waiting for her to be overwhelmed by fear.
Something climbs onto the back of her neck—

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Mm... ugh...
The nightmare left Magallan feeling sick. She wants to walk out the door, catch her breath, and calm herself down before going back to sleep.
But the moment she steps outside, what she sees makes her doubt that she has actually awoken from her dream.
There is a large, shadowy entity roaming here.
It looks like a person, and also kind of like a tree. The large shadow is moving in a single direction at a slow yet steady pace.
The entity shrouds even the moon above, keeping the ground below out of the moonlight's reach.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: What... is this?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I need to get a picture of it.
*Click*—

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Th-That's not possible. It makes no sense!
In the photo she just took, the shadow was nowhere to be seen and the moonlight illuminates the ground. Everything looks perfectly normal.
But the shadow stills moves before her eyes.
Without a sound.
Magallan stands rooted to the spot.
She doesn't know if she should head back inside to sleep as if nothing had happened...
...Or go grab her equipment and measure this possibly unrecordable supernatural phenomenon as best she can.
Just as she finds herself lost in thought, the enormous shadow sweeps past her. She instinctively jumps back, and at the same time—
Something climbs onto the back of her neck—

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: What are you doing out here?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Ah!

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: *sigh* Relax, Magallan. Calm down. I'm here. Nothing here is going to hurt you.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Huff... Haah... Phew...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Don't try talk yet. Calm down first.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Mmm...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Have a seat, and drink some water. It doesn't matter how big that guy is. It's just a shadow.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Huff... huff—

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Feeling any better?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Mm, thanks. You almost scared me to death.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: You're stronger than I expected. I was looking forward to you screaming loud enough to wake everyone up.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Are they going to kick me out of the village tonight, then?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: No, no. The Sami aren't that narrow-minded.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: ...Had a nightmare?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Let me guess. One where a beastling cub goes home, finds its mother's bones, and then gets eaten?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Did you have the same dream?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Yep. Just this afternoon in your sleeping bag.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I'm sorry...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: It's not your fault. It comes whenever I rest in a safe, relaxing environment.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Like an unwelcome friend.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: This is one of the bad things about Sami. The cycle of hunt or be hunted never ends, even in your dreams.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: And in dreams, most find themselves on the side of the hunted...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Then... can we become the hunters?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Wouldn't you rather be the rules themselves?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Is that even possible...?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Who knows?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Maybe it is.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Once we become more mature...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: When we're no longer afraid of these big guys.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Magallan, why don't we try touching it?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Huh? Isn't that dangerous?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I thought you were an explorer? Why are you so afraid?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I only ever set out after I've planned for every possible contingency, but how am I supposed to prepare for this?!

spans.text: I only ever set out after I've planned for every possible contingency, but how am I supposed to prepare for

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: S-Stop pulling—

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Aghhh! We stepped on the tree!

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: It's not the main trunk. Stepping on it a little won't hurt.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Besides, no one's around to see.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Hup.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: This is a great spot. Let's sit here.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: A-Are you sure we're not too close?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: How are we supposed to touch it from far away?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Are we... really going to touch it?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: It's just a shadow. There's nothing to be scared of.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Or to exact, it's only a shadow for now. A very, very faint one.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Maybe one day it will grow into a more concrete threat, but we'll have grown too. We'll have even more tricks up our sleeves.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: So when that time comes, maybe these things won't be so scary to us anymore.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Besides, I can sometimes hear a voice in that dream where we're preyed on.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: 'If something ever scares you, you should attack it without hesitation.'

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: 'If you defeat it, you will have defeated fear. If you run from it, you will always be afraid.'

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Come.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: But...
Magallan uneasily looks at the curtain-like shadow before her.
The cruel and oppressive feeling she felt in her dream still haunts her mind.
Part of her tells her not to take the risk, but—
She slowly reaches her hand out.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Just like that. Slowly. It'll be fine.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I'll do it with you.
Typhon places her palm on the back of Magallan's hand and gently pushes it forward.
The moment they're met with a hint of resistance, she stops pushing forward, and instead reaches forward ahead of Magallan's hand.
She dips her hand into the shadow and pulls it back out. Then, she places it back on Magallan's hand.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: See? Nothing to be afraid of.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Mm... I'll give it a try...
Magallan's hand inches forward bit by bit, until her fingertips are finally submerged in the shadow.
She thought she would feel a hint of cold, or perhaps that something would suck her in or chew on her fingers.
But there was nothing.
Nothing.
First, up to a joint. Then, a whole finger. Finally, her whole hand.
The shadow still moves, but aside from the change in the light, nothing happens at all.
Exactly as Typhon said.
It's just a shadow.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: How is it? Just like I said, right?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: You're right... There's nothing.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hm... How did something like this happen in the first place...?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Still hung up on those scientific principles of yours?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Things don't just happen without rhyme or reason.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Mm-hm.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Then how come our mothers gave birth to you and me, and not to anybody else?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Based on your logic, isn't that something with no rhyme or reason?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: W-Well, that's because...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: It seems like you southerners really need to have a reason for everything.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: But if you ask me, I think it's more important to be able to face the unknown at any time.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Even if I'm not prepared.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Don't you... get scared?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Do you? When you encounter a blizzard in the icefield, an avalanche in the mountains, or a pack of beasts when you're alone?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I do, yeah... but I still think I'll manage to survive somehow.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: If you can manage to survive even when you're scared, you've already accomplished the most difficult thing there is.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: And in that case, what else is there to be afraid of?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Even if the shadow in front of us were to suddenly turn into a real monster, you wouldn't be afraid, would you?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: If it were something that actually exists, we could deal with it. This? This is just a shadow.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Everything that exists has a weak point.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: You wait, observe, and survive until the moment you find that weakness, and then you attack. That's how hunters have always lived.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: You're an explorer, so you're something like half a hunter. I'm sure you can handle these things, too.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Nothing stays the same forever. Maybe there will come a day when the things that once scared you are afraid of you instead.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Don't overthink it. We have to be on the road tomorrow.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Oh, right. Here.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Want a fruit before you go back to bed?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: No thanks. Eating sugar before bed is how you get cavities.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Alright, up to you.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Good night.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Nighty-night, Typhon.
Magallan turns around and looks at the hovering shadow once more.
But for some reason, she doesn't think it represents fear and emptiness this time.
It feels more like a traveler who has lost his bearings and doesn't know where to go. Simply wandering the lands aimlessly.
Maybe, by the time the sun rises, it will have gone back home for a good night's sleep.
*Click*—
Magallan takes another picture. Just like before, there is nothing in the photograph.
She thinks a little, and adds a note on the picture.
'Mr. Lonesome.'
Finally, everything is quiet once more.
Only the wandering shadow is left to hover around alone.
Until daybreak.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: It should almost be time.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I wonder what kind of ceremony this is.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Ooh, it's starting!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: (Takes out her notebook) 'The Sami begin the ceremony by singing and dancing around their clan tree. Perhaps this is meant to be a farewell to the tree.'
Ten minutes later...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'The dance is very unique, but disorderly. Everyone dances on their own.'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'It's almost like a carnival.'
Thirty minutes later...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: (Yawns)

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Is Simone here yet?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Oh, she's right under the tree, talking to the shaman.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: If you wanna look, I can lend you my binoculars.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: No thanks. My eyes are enough to see her without your gadget.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: What kind of ceremony is this, anyway? And how much longer will it take? If you hadn't come, I'd have fallen asleep by now.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I'm a Sami Sarkaz, not a Sami Elafia. I don't know much more than you.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: As for how long it will take, that's hard to say. I've seen ceremonies that ended with just the shaman's nod, as well as gatherings that lasted all day and night.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: But forget the ceremony. Take a look at this. I found it in the forest!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Is this... a snowball?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: It's Amma's Affection, Magallan! This is Amma's Affection!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Amma? That means 'mother,' right?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Good memory.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: As a southerner might put it, this is a mother's love.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: It's the protection most sought after by the Sami. Among all of Sami's kindnesses, it's the purest and most sincere.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Here, take it Magallan. Put it in your pocket.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Didn't you just say all the Sami want this? You found it, so you should keep it. I can't take it.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I know its worth, but that's why I don't have the right to it.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Amma doesn't like granting protection to greedy people.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: But you know nothing about her. Ignorance is also a kind of purity, and you have an honest soul. That's why you should have it.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Then... what should I do with it?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Forget about it, like you never received it in the first place.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Then I gotta give you something in return, too.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hold on...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Here you go, Li'l Typhoon.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: What did you just call me?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: ...Never mind. So what is this?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: A flare. Just twist open the lid and pull the string, and it'll let out a ton of light and noise. You're a hunter; I'm sure can think of a use.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: That does sound pretty useful. I'll try it out next time.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Huh? Magallan, they stopped dancing. Aren't you taking notes? Quick!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Huh? Oh! Okay!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: (Pulls out notebook) 'After forty straight minutes of independent carnival, the ceremony has moved onto its next phase.'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'The shaman shows the tribesmen a woodcarving.'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'She says something impassioned.'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'Then, she raises her wooden staff, faces the clan tree, and sounds the horn. Then she starts murmuring something.'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'There is another shaman assisting her by her side, like she is singing an accompaniment.'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Typhon, can you help me out and figure out what they're saying?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I can't understand it.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: The tone is familiar, but those are clearly not words you use in normal conversation.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: (Jots notes) 'Some sort of ritualistic language.'

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: She's repeating a few short words over and over.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'Repeating...'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'Her emotions build up, and she keeps raising her voice—'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: W-What's going on?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: An earthquake? Typhon?! Where should we evacuate to?!

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: No... Magallan...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Look... The tree...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: (In Sarkaz) My god.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hmm...?
The tree's roots begin to emerge as it gradually lifts off the ground.
A thunderous sound rings through the forest and suppresses the shouts of everyone underneath.
Surrounded by other trees, it slowly rises into the air as its roots wring together into a bundle and form an unprecedented—in human terms—mobile structure.
Its leaves come falling down from the canopy, but the Sami are not shocked in the slightest. Instead, they appear very excited.
Indeed, what could be more encouraging than your tribe's ancestral tree lifting itself from the ground along with all the clan's history and memories?

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (In Sami) Congratulations, Attendant. The ritual was a success.

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) I've always thought my ancestors' journey with the Tree was a mere tale.

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) Thank you, child of the Santalla Tree. Without your interpretation and assistance, this awakening ceremony would not have been successful.

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) The Tree has awakened, but It still awaits a direction and Its next steps from us. I must research our tribe register more.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (In Sami) With the Tree's enormous body out in the open, the disaster of the north is bound to notice it.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (In Sami) Their activity has been growing more and more frequent of late. You must pray for Sami to protect the Tree with you.

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) Yes. Yes, you are right.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (In Sami) Please make your way to the south with all haste and replant the Tree. Do not let yourselves get caught up in them.

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) Understood. Hm... The register says...

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (In Sami) Well, then. My companions and I must take our leave. I pray that Sami will find you and your tribe a satisfactory destination, such that you need never relocate again.

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) Oh, are you leaving so soon?

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (In Sami) You still have much to attend to. No need to see us off.

steps.name: Forest Shaman
steps.text: (In Sami) Then I wish you and your companions a safe and uneventful journey. Once again, I thank you kindly for your help, honored friend... Oh... I see... To make the Tree set out, I must first...

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (In Sami) Farewell.
Report.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (Imitating the Ursus Messenger's voice) I have entered Sami as planned. Please advise on the positions of Liebafowl and the Black Mark. Over.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Hmph...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Simone, Simone!

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Yeah, I'm back.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Is there something I can help you with?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: It's time to go.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: I'm sorry that took so long.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: It's okay. Let's go.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Simone, you really need to explain to me what she said during the ritual. It's going to be real important to my research!

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: I'll tell you all about it on the way.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Sounds good.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: What's the matter?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Nothing. I'll be done real quick!
*Click*—
Before she leaves, Magallan snaps a picture of the enormous tree standing in the forest.
For some reason, she feels that this gigantic being almost completely blocking the sun looks kind of familiar—
She doesn't think too much about it, and merely scribbles her immediate thoughts into her notebook.
Then, she follows the rest of the group and continue their journey to southern Sami.
